title: Selective conformal inference with false coverage-statement rate control
headline: Open finding: the lower FCR bound printed in Theorem 2, equation (9), is false as stated because it uses a raw score order statistic where the proof requires the PIT/CDF probability.

work.title: Selective conformal inference with false coverage-statement rate control

claims.label: Theorem 2 equation (9) lower FCR bound
claims.page: Biometrika 111(3), 727–742, Section 4.2, Theorem 2, equation (9); current-author PDF physical p. 9
claims.gist: The printed lower false coverage-statement rate bound uses the raw score order statistic T_(khat+1), although the proof’s binomial probability is on the PIT/CDF scale F_T(T_(khat+1)).
claims.statement: Theorem 2, equation (9), states a lower FCR bound using the raw score order statistic T_(khat+1) where the proof requires the probability-scale quantity F_T(T_(khat+1)).
conditions: Independent and identically distributed calibration and test data under the theorem’s ranking-based selection assumptions.
The scores T_i=g(X_i) are real-valued on their raw scale; the theorem does not require them to lie in [0,1].
claims.quantifiers: The stated class of ranking-based selection procedures and score distributions.

result.summary: A continuous bounded-support example makes the printed lower endpoint approximately 14.147, exceeding 1. Translating every score by 100.01 preserves ranks, selected units, conformal intervals and actual FCR, yet leaves a printed lower endpoint approximately 0.09909094 above the actual FCR of 1/33.
result.witness: Take n=10 calibration observations and m=2 test observations, Top-1 selection, k=1, alpha=0.1, score map g(x)=x and predictor zero. Independently draw X from Uniform(-0.01,-0.005) and Y from Uniform(0,1). With M=T_(2), the printed lower endpoint is approximately 14.147, greater than 1. After translating every score by 100.01, the actual FCR remains 1/33, while the printed endpoint is approximately 0.09909094.
result.argument: The proof converts raw scores to their probability-integral-transform values and uses the threshold probability F_T(M) in its binomial calculation. The raw threshold M is not itself that probability, so substituting M makes the printed expression depend on the arbitrary score scale. In the continuous bounded-support example the endpoint exceeds 1. Positive translation leaves ranks, selected units, conformal intervals and actual FCR unchanged but makes the printed endpoint exceed the actual FCR. The lower-bound correction is to use F_T(M), or an equivalent probability-scale quantity. This finding does not challenge the SCOP upper guarantee, the SCOP procedure itself, or the empirical results.
not_claimed: The SCOP upper guarantee is false.
The SCOP procedure itself is invalid.
result.repair_note: Use F_T(M), or an equivalent probability-scale quantity, in place of the raw order statistic M in the lower-bound calculation.

vor_check.pages: Biometrika 111(3), 727–742, Section 4.2, Theorem 2, equation (9); current-author PDF physical p. 9; proof supplement Section C.1.
vor_check.detail: The DOI-linked current-author theorem and proof-bearing supplement were checked. The subscriber-restricted typeset VOR theorem page was not independently displayed, so VOR verification remains partial.

evidence.detail: A fresh hostile validation reproduced the raw-score/PIT mismatch, the continuous negative-support endpoint above 1, and the positive-translation example in which the printed endpoint exceeds the unchanged actual FCR. It did not refute the SCOP upper guarantee or the rank-based procedure.
